title: Plant metabolite shows promise as natural sunscreen that blocks UV light
content: Research published in Photochemistry and Photobiology reports that a plant‑derived metabolite capable of blocking ultraviolet light shows promising potential as a natural sunscreen when applied to human skin.
summary: Research published in Photochemistry and Photobiology reports that a plant metabolite can block the effects of ultraviolet light. The study suggests the metabolite has promising potential as a natural sunscreen when applied to human skin.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists discover 15,000‑lb baby right whale off Canada
content: Scientists have discovered an unknown baby right whale off Canada, a find that has delighted researchers who study rare whales. The newborn weighs 15,000 pounds (6,804 kilograms). After months of searching, the team reports they are “couldn’t be happier” with the discovery.
summary: Scientists studying rare whales discovered an unknown baby right whale off Canada. The calf weighs about 15,000 pounds (6,804 kilograms) and the researchers said they are very happy about the find.
author: Phys.org

title: Pakistani astronaut to join Shenzhou 24, first foreigner on China's space station
content: A Pakistani astronaut is scheduled to join the crew of China’s Shenzhou 24 spacecraft, a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing’s space station, state media reported on Saturday.
summary: A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft. The mission would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.
author: Phys.org

title: Polar vortex falters weeks earlier than ever recorded, meteorologists say
content: Meteorologists reported on Friday that they are observing an unprecedented early disruption of the polar vortex, occurring weeks earlier than any previously recorded event. The anomaly is said to increase the risk of cold snaps across the Northern Hemisphere, although significant uncertainty remains about its impacts.
summary: Meteorologists said on Friday they were observing an unprecedented early disruption of the polar vortex. They noted it raises the risk of cold snaps across the Northern Hemisphere, though significant uncertainty remains.
author: Phys.org

title: Diwali celebrations in northern India align with hazardous winter air
content: Diwali festivities across South Asia, particularly in northern India, are occurring alongside the onset of hazardous winter air. The overlap has prompted concerns about how to observe the holiday safely amid the deteriorating air quality.
summary: Diwali festivities across South Asia, particularly in northern India, coincide with the return of hazardous winter air. This overlap raises concerns about how to celebrate safely.
author: Phys.org

title: Ancient Lambayeque societies stayed peaceful despite El Niño floods and sacrifices
content:
Archaeologists investigating past climate change have identified instances of human sacrifice linked to extreme weather. In northern Peru’s desert coast, mass ritual sacrifices were associated with catastrophic flooding caused by El Niño, prompting questions about whether such rites reflected a broader surge in violence driven by resource scarcity.

However, a recent survey of the Lambayeque Valley indicates that, despite these sacrificial events, overall violence in the region was extremely rare even during periods of ecological upheaval. The findings suggest that ancient societies in the area remained generally peaceful despite facing severe climate‑related disruptions.
summary: Archaeologists have linked mass ritual sacrifices along the desert coast of northern Peru to catastrophic flooding caused by El Niño. A new survey of the Lambayeque Valley indicates that violence was extremely rare even during periods of ecological upheaval.
author: Phys.org

title: MIT/NYU FLEX platform lets robots infer higher-level intent from natural language
content:
MIT and New York University researchers have unveiled FLEX, a flexible feature‑editing pipeline that lets robots interpret natural, conversational language commands and extend those instructions beyond their literal wording. The system was presented this month at the annual Conference on Robot Learning and is designed to improve robot motion‑planning by allowing a human to give high‑level directives that the robot can reason about and apply to its environment.

In a series of simulated trials, a virtual robotic arm was tasked with moving objects such as a cup of coffee, a candle, and a bowling ball. Participants typed commands like “Don’t spill on my laptop,” “Stay away from the stack of paper,” or “Don’t drop on the mug.” FLEX enabled the robot to follow each instruction literally while also inferring broader rules—avoiding electronics, flammable items, and fragile objects—without the user having to list every detail.

The core of FLEX is a large language model, GPT‑4o, which the robot consults during the “Generalize” step. The model scans its extensive training data to find patterns linking the user’s specified features (e.g., a laptop or a mug) to related categories such as electronics or fragile items. This common‑sense reasoning allows the robot to add new constraints automatically.

FLEX operates in three phases that take roughly five seconds. First, “Add” places the user‑identified feature on a list of relevant objects. Second, “Generalize” uses the LLM to expand that list based on learned associations. Third, “Mask” employs the robot’s vision system to remove objects that are no longer present, keeping the feature list current.

The study was led by Andreea Bobu, assistant professor of aeronautics and astronautics at MIT, with co‑authors Audrey Lee SM ’26 and Ilia Sucholutsky of New York University. Bobu directs MIT’s Collaborative Learning and Autonomy Research (CLEAR) Lab, which focuses on autonomous agents that can learn and adapt to human preferences. The work received partial support from the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium and the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing’s Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing program.
summary: MIT and New York University researchers introduced FLEX, a flexible feature‑editing pipeline that lets robots interpret natural language commands and generalize to avoid electronics, fragile items, and other hazards. The platform, demonstrated in simulated scenarios such as a robot serving coffee, was presented at the annual Conference on Robot Learning.
author: MIT News

title: WorldParticle: MIT-UBC AI model simulates multiple physical phenomena
content:
A new deep‑learning system called WorldParticle is being presented as a single AI model that can simulate a wide range of physical phenomena, from sliding sand to folding proteins. The work is the result of a collaboration among researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the University of British Columbia (UBC), and several other institutions. The team describes the model as a “foundation model” for simulation that could replace the current practice of building separate, hand‑coded solvers for each type of material or process.

WorldParticle represents any material as a collection of tiny three‑dimensional particles using a Lagrangian formulation. A neural network receives the particles’ positions and physical properties as inputs and predicts their positions and properties for the next simulation step. The system separates external forces, makes an initial prediction, and then reintegrates those forces to correct the particle states, allowing it to adapt to new materials, forces, and environments that were not part of its training set.

To keep the computation tractable when objects are broken into millions of particles, the researchers incorporated a merging technique that compresses particles while preserving fine‑grained detail. The model was tested on six different physical phenomena, including deformable objects, granular materials and protein dynamics. In these tests WorldParticle achieved higher accuracy than conventional numerical simulators; for example, it correctly captured the collapse of a granular pile where baseline methods left particles floating, and it simulated protein structural changes about 100 times faster than existing numerical approaches.

The research team, led by Peter Yichen Chen (assistant professor at UBC) and Minghao Guo (MIT postdoc), includes graduate students Caoliwen Wang and Siyuan Chen, MIT professor Wojciech Matusik, and collaborators from Georgia Tech, Inria, Meta, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Utah, UCLA and the University of Hong Kong. The findings will be presented at the ACM SIGGRAPH Conference and Exhibition on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques in Asia. The authors envision extending WorldParticle to additional domains such as soft‑robot manipulation, RNA evolution and astrophysical processes, with the longer‑term goal of creating a general‑purpose simulation pipeline for scientific discovery.
summary: Today, a scientist who wants to simulate a physical process must pick the right tool for that one job, such as a solver built for flowing water or another designed to model the way a protein folds. Each one is hand-coded around the specific equations that dictate how that process behaves.
author: MIT News

title: Scientists isolate stable boron‑oxygen molecules after 60‑year mystery
content: Scientists have isolated stable examples of boron‑oxygen molecules that had been deemed too unstable to capture, ending more than 60 years of unsuccessful attempts. The breakthrough was achieved with relatively simple chemical reactions and is reported to open the possibility of a new class of exotic compounds.
summary: Scientists have finally isolated stable examples of elusive boron‑oxygen molecules that were previously thought too unstable to capture. The breakthrough, achieved with relatively simple chemical reactions, could open a new class of exotic compounds.
author: Science Daily

title: Dock leaves unlikely to uniquely relieve nettle stings, says Imperial professor
content: It’s a time-honoured treatment and rubbing certainly helps, but other leaves could be just as good If you’ve ever brushed against a stinging nettle, chances are someone told you to find a dock leaf. The wide green leaves of dock plants seem to grow conveniently nearby, and rubbing one on a sting is a time-honoured remedy. But does it actually work? Probably not in any way that’s unique to the plant, says John Tregoning, a professor at Imperial College London and the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death.
summary: Rubbing dock leaves on nettle stings is a long‑standing remedy that many people use. Professor John Tregoning of Imperial College London says the relief is probably not unique to dock leaves and other leaves could work as well.
author: Guardian Science

title: Great Square of Pegasus used to gauge sky darkness in London view at 2000 GMT, 9 Nov
content:
Starwatch will guide viewers in locating the Great Square of Pegasus and using its inner stars as an indicator of sky darkness. The segment explains that while the square’s four corner stars are broadly visible, counting the fainter interior stars provides a practical measure of how dark the sky is at a given location.

A chart accompanying the episode shows the view looking south from London at 2000 GMT on 9 November, with the Great Square of Pegasus positioned high in the sky as the distinctive four‑star pattern marking the mythical winged horse’s body.
summary: The Great Square of Pegasus’s four corners are widely visible, and its inner stars are used as an indicator of darkness by counting them. A chart shows the view looking south from London at 2000 GMT on 9 November, with the square high in the sky.
author: Guardian Science

title: 2026 Antarctic ozone hole reaches seventh‑largest area on September 18
content:
The NASA Earth Observatory has released a new data visualization that shows the area and shape of the Antarctic ozone hole on September 18, 2026, the day the hole reaches its annual maximum extent. Scientists define the ozone hole as the region where ozone concentrations fall below the historical threshold of 220 Dobson units (DU). The image, produced by Lauren Dauphin, is part of an update to the Observatory’s “World of Change” series that documents how Earth changes over time.

The visualization is based on satellite measurements taken from 1979 through 2026. From 1979‑2004 the data came from NASA’s Total Ozone Mapping Spectrometer (TOMS) on Nimbus‑7 and other satellites; from 2005‑2011 the Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) on the Aura satellite was used; from 2012‑2025 the Ozone Mapping and Profiler Suite (OMPS) on the Suomi NPP satellite provided the data; and in 2026 OMPS on the NOAA‑20 satellite supplied the latest observations. The map shows red and yellow areas indicating the ozone hole, with the word “hole” used metaphorically because no place is truly empty of ozone.

The 2026 hole was the seventh largest in the 48‑year record of monitoring, measured by its mean size from September 7 to October 13, the peak ozone‑depletion season. It was not as deep as some of the larger holes on record, but an unusually strong Antarctic polar vortex created ideal conditions for ozone depletion over a large area. Year‑to‑year variations in the hole’s area and depth are driven by changes in stratospheric temperature and circulation; colder conditions produce a larger area and lower ozone values in the core of the hole.

The Observatory’s article traces the history of the ozone hole, noting that before 1979 no ozone concentrations below 220 DU had been observed. In 1985, ground‑based measurements at Halley Research Station first reported dramatic thinning of the Antarctic stratosphere, and NASA satellite data revealed the continental scale of the depletion. The hole’s depth fell below 100 DU for the first time in 1991, and the deepest hole occurred in 1994 when concentrations dropped to 73 DU. The longest‑recorded largest hole occurred in 2006.

The article also summarizes the broader context of ozone‑depleting substances. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) released into the troposphere persist for decades and, once reaching the stratosphere, break apart under ultraviolet light to release chlorine, which catalyzes ozone destruction. Human‑produced chlorine accounts for about 80 % of the chlorine in the stratosphere today, while bromine compounds also contribute. The Montreal Protocol of 1987 phased out the production of these chemicals, and satellite evidence from 2018 showed a 20 % decrease in ozone depletion during the Antarctic winter months from 2005 to 2016. Models predict that the Antarctic ozone layer will return to 1980 levels in the 2070s.
summary: The Antarctic ozone hole reached its annual maximum area on September 18, 2026, measured by the OMPS instrument on the NOAA‑20 satellite. The 2026 hole was the seventh‑largest in 48 years of monitoring, though its depth was less than that of other large holes on record.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 9 2026 – Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula (IC 2118)
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 9 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula’s shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch’s head. Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation. What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to — because it has been partly eroded by — the nearby star Rigel. One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image. The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel’s intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth’s daytime sky to appear blue, although the scatterers in planet Earth’s atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. title: Flide inference engine speeds Jev-like decision models up to 9.5× faster
content:
Flide is a new inference engine designed specifically for Jev‑like decision models. The developers say that decision models require their own inference engine, so they created Flide to provide high‑performance, exact inference for this class of models.

According to the announcement, Flide delivers up to a 9.5‑fold speed improvement over the popular vLLM and SGLang engines. It also supports more than 30 widely used local Jev‑like decision models.

Users can install Flide immediately with `pip install flide`. The Show HN post (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50421155) has 25 points and 4 comments.
summary: Flide is a high‑performance exact inference engine for Jev‑like decision models that delivers up to a 9.5× speedup over vLLM and SGLang. It supports 30+ popular local Jev‑like decision models and can be installed with pip install flide.
author: Hacker News

title: Bikers and insect enthusiasts unite to block Google data center east of London
content: Protest activity over data centers is spreading across Europe, and a diverse coalition of campaigners—including bikers and bug‑lovers—is working to stop Google from constructing a large new data‑center facility east of London. The group’s aim is to block the project.
summary: A diverse group of bikers and insect enthusiasts has joined protests against a new Google data center. The campaigners are trying to block Google from building a sprawling facility east of London as protests spread across Europe.
author: Wired

title: Nvidia board probes Jensen Huang's ties to suspected Chinese spy, 50‑50 job outlook
content: Nvidia’s board is conducting an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang concerning his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld has said the likelihood that Huang will remain in his role is roughly a 50‑50 chance.
summary: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld says the likelihood of Huang remaining CEO is roughly a 50‑50 chance.
author: TechCrunch

title: England hospitals at 95% adult bed occupancy during peak flu season
content:
The piece warns that relentless streamlining can create hidden dangers, using England’s hospital capacity as a case in point. During the peak of last year’s flu season, about 95 % of adult hospital beds were occupied, a level that would be praised as efficient if hospitals were treated like hotels.  

The article argues that such high occupancy leaves little reserve capacity, meaning a single severe flu week could force treatment to be shifted into corridors. It suggests that the drive to optimise every system—from traffic roundabouts to financial markets—may backfire when it eliminates the buffers needed to handle unexpected spikes in demand.
summary: In England, about 95% of adult hospital beds were occupied at the height of flu season last year. The article warns that such high occupancy leaves little reserve capacity and could force treatment in corridors.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ‘Thicky thicky dumb dumb’ satirist Cody Dahler on his viral videos: ‘my material is presented to me on a silver platter!’
content: The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform. Given that I have zero rhythm, comedy was my other option. She wrote me a poem called Mrs Brown’s Moggy, about a cat that was often very soggy, for my school’s talent show. Because you can’t tell the difference between real and polite laughter at the age of six, I assumed I’d killed my first gig and convinced myself I was born to do nothing else. Where do you find your material? In a world where Robert Jenrick claims Nigel Farage has “ probably done more than almost anybody to stand against racism ”, the answer is that my material is presented to me on a silver platter each morning.
summary: The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform.
author: Guardian Technology

title: MP Ben Coleman urges NHS not to extend Palantir contract ending March
content:
Labour MP Ben Coleman, who represents Chelsea and Fulham and sits on the health and social care committee, warned that public confidence in Palantir is low and argued that the NHS should move away from its reliance on the U.S. firm. He noted that Palantir’s £330 million contract to operate NHS England’s federated data platform is set to expire next March, and that ministers must decide by Christmas whether to extend the agreement.

Coleman said the committee recommended no extension, citing contested benefits and the availability of alternative tools that could provide similar functionality. He urged a transition to new suppliers that would give the NHS full control of its technology and patient data. While acknowledging the appeal of appointing a single British firm, he cautioned that such a choice would not guarantee the NHS the flexibility to change suppliers without losing the systems it has built.
summary: MP Ben Coleman urges NHS not to extend Palantir contract ending March.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged affair with Chinese spy
content:
Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after reports described him as the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”  

Huang acknowledged an intimate relationship with a business executive who is alleged to have been spying on behalf of China.
summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, is being investigated by the company's board after reports he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Huang admitted to an intimate relationship with a business executive alleged to have been spying on behalf of China.
author: Euronews

title: Trump plans possible meeting with Putin and Xi in China next week
content: US President Donald Trump announced that he may meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China next week. He said the prospective talks would focus on “denuclearisation” and on ways to end the war in Iran.
summary: US President Donald Trump said he may meet Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China next week. He said the talks would cover denuclearisation and how to end the Iran war.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina, welcomed by President Javier Milei
content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday, 8 November, marking the first papal visit to the nation in nearly four decades. President Javier Milei greeted the pontiff at Buenos Aires airport, and the city’s iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honor.
summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday 8 November, marking the first papal visit in nearly 40 years. President Javier Milei greeted him at Buenos Aires airport and the city's iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honor.
author: Euronews

title: Dakar surf school expands wave access for local children
content: A surf school on Dakar’s beaches is working to make surfing accessible to local children. The school’s founder, Ibra Samb, who learned to surf on plywood, says his aim is to inspire a new generation of African surfers.
summary: On the beaches of Dakar, a surf school is making the waves accessible to local children. Founder Ibra Samb, who learnt to surf on plywood, hopes to inspire a new generation.
author: Euronews

title: Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calls him “honorable guy” after spy allegations
content: US President Donald Trump has defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he had an intimate relationship with a businesswoman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Trump said Huang was an "honorable guy".
summary: Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calls him “honorable guy” after spy allegations.
author: Euronews

title: G7 foreign ministers to discuss Ukraine war and US Iran strike options in Paris
content:
G7 foreign ministers will reconvene in Paris on Monday to revisit Russia’s war in Ukraine and discuss the prospect of further U.S. strikes on Iran. The agenda reflects ongoing concerns about the conflict in Ukraine and the possibility of additional American military action against Tehran.

Washington has kept the option of new strikes open since Republicans lost the midterm elections. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to attend both days of the Paris talks, a change from the March meeting where he participated for only one day.
summary: G7 foreign ministers will revisit Russia’s war in Ukraine and the prospect of further US strikes on Iran when they meet in Paris on Monday. Washington has kept the option of new strikes open since Republicans lost the midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Poland braces for tense week after deadliest Krakow shooting kills six
content: Poland is entering a tense week after a shooting in Krakow on Saturday, the deadliest in the country in decades, killed six people and wounded dozens. The incident has amplified worries about rising far‑right extremism as the nation prepares for an upcoming major nationalist march.
summary: Poland faces a week of political tensions after its deadliest shooting in decades left six people dead and dozens wounded in Krakow on Saturday. The attack has heightened concerns over rising far‑right extremism ahead of a major nationalist march.
author: France 24

title: Trump says deportation crackdown was “too tough” after midterm losses
content: US President Donald Trump said his administration's mass deportation campaign may have been "too tough" in a television interview aired Sunday, days after Republicans suffered heavy losses in midterm elections.
summary: US President Donald Trump said his administration's mass deportation campaign may have been "too tough". He made the remarks in a television interview aired Sunday, days after Republicans suffered heavy losses in the midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Daryna, 25, balances daily life with air raids and subway shelters in Kyiv
content: Daryna, 25, entered adulthood in a country at war. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion, her days have been shaped by air raid alerts, power outages and nights spent sheltering in the subway. Despite the uncertainty that shadows every day, she is determined to preserve a semblance of normal life in Kyiv. FRANCE 24 met a young woman who has become emblematic of a generation learning to live under daily bombardment.
summary: Daryna, 25, lives in Kyiv where her days are marked by air raid alerts, power outages and nights sheltering in the subway since Russia’s full-scale invasion. She says she is determined to preserve a semblance of normal life, and FRANCE 24 describes her as emblematic of a generation learning to live under daily bombardment.
author: France 24

title: New Zealand election too close to call as over 95% of votes counted
content: Initial results in New Zealand’s election, with more than 95% of votes tallied, show the two main parties virtually tied, separated by fewer than 4,000 votes. The final, official outcome will not be released until later this month after special votes are counted.
summary: Initial results show the two main parties neck‑and‑neck with fewer than 4,000 votes separating them. Official results aren’t expected until later this month once special votes have been counted.
author: DW World

title: Krakow shooting suspect dies in hospital after police shootout
content: Police in Poland say the alleged gunman responsible for killing six people in a shooting spree in Krakow has died in hospital from injuries sustained during a shootout with police.
summary: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in Krakow died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police. Police in Poland said the suspect died in hospital.
author: DW World

title: Gen Z protests challenge authoritarianism in Brazil, Serbia and worldwide
content:
Young people in Serbia, Bangladesh, India, France and Brazil are confronting what they see as authoritarianism and altering political dynamics. In Brazil, activists organized massive online rallies, sharing videos and memes, while Serbian youths travelled by bicycle across Europe and completed ultramarathons to amplify their message.

Both the Serbian and Brazilian actions entered the international spotlight last month, becoming focal points in election campaigns that highlighted resistance to authoritarian rule. Observers describe these developments as part of a broader, worldwide pattern of youth‑led movements reshaping political landscapes.
summary: From Serbia to Bangladesh and India to France, young people are pushing back against authoritarianism and reshaping political landscapes In Brazil, they rallied online by the millions, sharing videos and spreading memes. In Serbia, they cycled across Europe and ran ultramarathons to make their voices heard.
author: Guardian World

title: French police officers to stand trial for beating of black music producer over mask violation
content:
Three French police officers are set to stand trial for the 2020 beating of Michel Zecler, a 47‑year‑old Black music producer who police said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic. The case is described as a rare instance of police brutality reaching a courtroom amid heightened tensions.

The assault sparked outrage in France, with victims and researchers characterising police violence as systemic, while authorities and law‑enforcement unions maintain that such incidents are isolated.
summary: Three French police officers will stand trial for beating Michel Zecler, a 47‑year‑old black music producer, after he was accused of not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic. The assault sparked outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers describe as systemic while authorities say it is limited to isolated cases.
author: Guardian World

title: Poland justice minister says Kraków shooting probe will assess if 24‑year‑old acted alone
content: Poland’s justice minister said the investigation into the Kraków shooting will focus on determining whether the 24‑year‑old attacker acted alone. Authorities opened a terrorism investigation after the gunman opened fire in a market square in Kraków, the country’s second‑largest city. The weekend attack left six people dead. The attacker, a 24‑year‑old Polish national, was wounded in a shootout with police and has now died in hospital, officials confirmed.
summary: A terrorism investigation was opened after a 24‑year‑old Polish attacker opened fire in a market square in Kraków, killing six people. The attacker, injured in a shootout with police, later died in hospital, and the justice minister said the probe will determine whether he acted alone.
author: Guardian World

title: NSW Premier Chris Minns calls One Nation's Stuart Bonds comments 'outrageous and racist'
content: Chris Minns and race discrimination commissioner lambast comments made by Stuart Bonds, who leads party’s NSW upper house ticket Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The New South Wales premier and the Australian Human Rights Commission have criticised comments by the man who heads One Nation’s upper house ticket in NSW after he said Australians faced demographic replacement unless “mass migration” was curtailed. Chris Minns described Stuart Bonds’ comments as “frankly outrageous and racist”.
summary: NSW Premier Chris Minns calls One Nation's Stuart Bonds comments 'outrageous and racist'.
author: Guardian World

title: Royal commission hears CFMEU wields influence over Victorian government in Sunbury project
content: Inquiry into allegations of corruption begins block of hearings focused on 2022 level crossing removal project Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The royal commission into allegations of corruption on Victorian Big Build projects has heard a major construction company feared putting the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU) offside because of its close links to the Daniel Andrews Labor government. The first block of hearings under the commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria will hear evidence about the union’s involvement in a level crossing removal project at Gap Road in Sunbury, north of Melbourne, in 2022.
summary: The Victorian Big Build royal commission began a block of hearings on the 2022 Gap Road level‑crossing removal project in Sunbury. A major construction company told the commission it feared alienating the CFMEU because of the union’s close links to the Daniel Andrews Labor government.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian Labor poll at 18% trailing One Nation and Coalition ahead of 2026 election
content:
Victorian Labor MPs have expressed both scepticism and serious concern after a new opinion poll ahead of the 2026 state election showed the party falling to an all‑time low in primary‑vote support. The DemosAU/PremierNational poll, first published by the Herald Sun on Monday, recorded Labor at 18%, placing it third behind the Coalition’s 33% and One Nation’s 21%.

Labor leader Ben Carroll declined to comment on the poll’s findings. The same survey indicated that the Greens increased their primary‑vote share to 17%, a rise of three points since September. The results suggest a significant shift in voter preferences as the election approaches.
summary: Victorian Labor poll at 18% trailing One Nation and Coalition ahead of 2026 election.
author: Guardian World

title: Environment Minister Murray Watt urges Labor colleagues not to undermine Treasurer Jim Chalmers
content:
Environment minister Murray Watt told his colleagues that they should stop “undermining” Treasury chief Jim Chalmers as the Labor government works to sell its budget. Watt said the party is facing pressure to cut popular clean‑energy subsidies in an effort to combat inflation.

Cabinet ministers reconvened on Monday to discuss possible budget savings that could be incorporated into next month’s mid‑year update, part of a broader push to reduce spending and ease economic pressure. Watt added that “all sorts of people” are making comments about the process.
summary: Murray Watt told Labor ministers to stop undermining Treasurer Jim Chalmers as the party works to sell its budget and consider cuts to clean energy subsidies. Cabinet ministers met on Monday to discuss potential budget savings for the next month’s mid-year update to reduce spending and ease inflation pressure.
author: Guardian World

title: Pope Leo rebukes President Milei's austerity measures in Buenos Aires
content:
Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s austerity measures during his visit to Argentina, the second stop of a 12‑day Latin America tour. He said, “The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” insisting that growth must benefit all.

The Pope’s remarks were met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires. He made the statement shortly after landing in Argentina on Sunday.
summary: Pope Leo XIV criticized Argentine President Javier Milei's austerity measures, saying the economy must serve the people. He delivered the remarks on Sunday after arriving in Buenos Aires for the second leg of a 12‑day Latin America tour, receiving applause.
author: Guardian World

title: Dalot's poor form highlights Manchester United's chaos and 18th-place finish
content:
Manchester United’s recent struggles have cast Diogo Dalot, the stand-in left-back, in the role of a pantomime villain, although fans are reportedly struggling to direct their frustration at him specifically. The article characterizes the club’s situation as a global soap opera, where sporting success has become nearly irrelevant to the organization’s massive brand and revenue streams. This shift has transformed the football club into a source of dramatic entertainment, featuring a cast that includes billionaire owners and an under-pressure manager.

The narrative highlights the absurdity of current events, describing Dalot’s muddled performances as just one symptom of the broader chaos at Old Trafford. Amidst these larger-than-life figures, the article identifies "petty culprits" responsible for relegating Manchester United to 18th place in the Premier League. This sporting decline has left manager Michael Carrick questioning how much longer he can survive in his role.
summary: Diogo Dalot's muddled performances as stand-in left-back are described as a symptom of the broader chaos at Old Trafford. Manchester United currently sits in 18th place in the Premier League, with manager Michael Carrick facing significant pressure.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emma Peschel scores on debut as USA beats Germany 5-0 in women's hockey world championship
content:
Emma Peschel scored on her international debut as the United States defeated Germany 5-0 in a Group A match at the women’s ice hockey world championship on Sunday. The 22-year-old defender recorded a goal with a wrist shot from the point, extending the American lead to 2-0 during the opening period.

The United States outscored their opponents 12-0 across their first two games of the tournament. Meanwhile, Sweden secured a 4-1 victory over Finland in a separate result.
summary: Emma Peschel scores on debut as USA beats Germany 5-0 in women's hockey world championship.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Kyle Larson Clinches Third Cup Title, First Back-to-
content:
Kyle Larson secured his third NASCAR Cup Series championship in six years during Sunday’s 400-mile season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. By clinching the title in the opening stage, the Hendrick driver became the first to win back-to-back championships since Jimmie Johnson in 2010. Johnson previously captured five consecutive titles starting in 2006.

Ryan Blaney won the season finale race at Homestead. Larson’s achievement places him among NASCAR’s all-time greats, marking a significant milestone in his career as a repeat champion.
summary: Kyle Larson Clinches Third Cup Title, First Back-to-.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia Selectors Drop Marnus Labuschagne from Test Squad
content:
Marnus Labuschagne has been dropped from Australia’s Test squad. Chairman of selectors George Bailey confirmed on Monday that the batter would be omitted from the yet‑to‑be‑named squad for the first Test against New Zealand.  

The next Test is scheduled to begin on 9 December in Perth, and Bailey and his panel have decided to exclude Labuschagne from consideration for the entire four‑Test series against New Zealand.  

Bailey told reporters that it remains possible the out‑of‑form star could be recalled for future tours to India and England.
summary: Marnus Labuschagne has been dropped from Australia’s Test squad for the series against New Zealand. Chairman of selectors George Bailey confirmed that he will not be considered for the entire four-Test series.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Barcelona Secures Top Spot with Fermín López Double vs Atlético Madrid
content:
Barcelona secured a 2-1 victory over Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano, maintaining their position at the top of the table. The match served as a significant test for Hansi Flick’s side, which had recently suffered defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. Despite a frenetic first half in which Barcelona trailed following a goal by Giuliano Simeone, the visitors found a way through to claim the win.

Fermín López was the decisive factor, scoring two goals either side of the break to overturn the deficit. The intense atmosphere at the stadium matched the high stakes of the encounter, which featured ten World Cup winners on the field. Ultimately, Barcelona held their nerve to secure a victory that not only earned them three points but also helped alleviate recent doubts about their form.
summary: Barcelona defeated Atlético Madrid 2-1 at the Metropolitano, with Fermín López scoring both goals. The win kept Barcelona at the top of the table.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Crystal Palace set to sack Pierre Sage, eye Thomas Frank after Liverpool loss
content:
Crystal Palace are preparing to dismiss manager Pierre Sage after a 1‑0 loss to Liverpool that pushed the club to the bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017. The Frenchman, who took over in mid‑June to replace Oliver Glasner, has faced mounting pressure following a 5‑0 defeat to Brighton and a run of four consecutive league losses.

With no signs of improvement, the club’s board has identified former Tottenham Hotspur manager Thomas Frank as the leading candidate to replace Sage. Frank’s name has surfaced as the main option for the role as Palace look to halt their slide in the standings.
summary: Crystal Palace are poised to sack French manager Pierre Sage after a Liverpool defeat that left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017. Former Spurs manager Thomas Frank is the main candidate to replace him.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England beat Australia 45-22; Itoje praises Borthwick as world‑class coach
content: ‘I’m delighted we got the win. He’s a world-class coach’ England beat Australia 45-22 in Nations Championship Maro Itoje, the England captain, has reiterated his squad’s full support for the head coach, Steve Borthwick, after the home side’s resounding 45-22 victory against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Itoje described Borthwick as “a world‑class coach” and said England were “lucky to have him” despite fresh media reports of unhappiness in the camp this summer. Borthwick also revealed he had received several pre-game messages from former England coaches urging him to ignore external criticism and to concentrate on the rugby. His team certainly succeeded in that regard, scoring seven tries to rack up a record number of points against the Wallabies and register only their third win in their past eight games.
summary: England defeated Australia 45-22 in the Nations Championship at Allianz Stadium. Captain Maro Itoje praised head coach Steve Borthwick as a world‑class coach and said England were lucky to have him, with the squad fully supporting him.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick denies risk of Manchester United sack after 4-4 draw with Aston Villa
content:
Michael Carrick dismissed speculation that he could resign as Manchester United head coach after the club’s chaotic 4‑4 draw with Aston Villa. When asked about talks over his position, the former midfielder replied, “Is there?” and insisted he expects to move forward.

The result left United in the bottom three, 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games. The team has won only once this season, a home victory over Ipswich in August, and has now gone eight league matches without a win—a club record. Carrick’s job remains in jeopardy amid the club’s poor run of form.
summary: Michael Carrick denied a suggestion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach after the club's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them in 18th place with eight points from 10 games. The match left United in the relegation zone and marked a club record of eight consecutive Premier League games without a win.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Falkirk rise to third in Scottish Premiership after five straight wins under John McGlynn
content: Falkirk continue to excel under the canny guidance of John McGlynn. A run of five successive victories has propelled the club up to third place in the Scottish Premiership. The team’s recent form underscores the rapid rise highlighted in the club’s latest achievements.
summary: Falkirk continue to excel under the canny guidance of John McGlynn. A run of five successive victories has taken them up to third in the Scottish Premiership.
author: BBC Sport

title: Premier League Table After 10 Games: What History Reveals
content: BBC Sport examines the Premier League table after 10 games, drawing on historical data to interpret the standings. The analysis focuses on what past seasons reveal about team positions at this early stage, offering insight into how the current table may evolve as the season progresses.
summary: BBC Sport examines the Premier League table after 10 games. It discusses what historical patterns suggest about the table at this point.
author: BBC Sport

title: Norris sparkles in Sao Paulo Grand Prix despite firework mishap
content: Lando Norris was virtually impeccable during the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, a race that pushed drivers to their limits. The only incident was that he got too close to a firework.
summary: Lando Norris was virtually impeccable during the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. He only got too close to a firework, while the race challenged drivers to their very limits.
author: BBC Sport

title: Iran issues 2‑day ultimatum to U.S.; Trump shares Dana White cartoon
content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X that “American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own.” He reiterated Iran’s 2‑day proposal, demanding the U.S. meet requirements, including ending war on all fronts, to see results.  

In a separate move, former President Donald Trump shared a cartoon depicting Dana White as a U.S. press secretary while he considers an offer.
summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday said on the social platform X that “American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own.” “Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results,” he added.
author: The Hill

title: Hamilton says many Kansans view Schumer as polarizing
content: Adam Hamilton, the newly elected Democratic Kansas senator, said Sunday that many people in Kansas view Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N. Y.) as “polarizing.” NBC News’s Kristen Welker asked Hamilton during his interview Sunday on “Meet the Press” why the top Senate Democrat, whom Hamilton has been critical of before, is not the right leader…
summary: Adam Hamilton, newly elected Democratic Kansas senator, said Sunday that many people in Kansas view Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer as “polarizing.” He was interviewed by NBC News’s Kristen Welker on “Meet the Press” and questioned why Schumer is not the right leader.
author: The Hill

title: Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Plant loses final power line, switches to emergency generators
content: A Ukrainian nuclear plant has lost its last external power line, forcing it to switch to emergency diesel generators. The Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) now relies on these generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security functions. The cause of the latest disconnection remains unknown.
summary: The Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) lost all off‑site power after its final external power line disconnected. The plant is now using emergency diesel generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security functions.
author: The Hill

title: Senator‑elect Abdul El‑Sayed calls Stephen Miller the most broken man to run White House
content: Abdul El-Sayed, the newly elected Democratic Michigan senator, on Sunday slammed Trump administration adviser and recently appointed White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, calling him the “most broken man.” During the senator-elect’s “This Week” appearance on Sunday, ABC News’s Jonathan Karl asked El-Sayed about “what message” Miller’s new role “sends to the country and…
summary: Abdul El‑Sayed, the newly elected Democratic Michigan senator, criticized Stephen Miller, a Trump administration adviser and newly appointed White House chief of staff, on Sunday. He said Miller is the most broken man and will run the most dysfunctional White House.
author: The Hill

title: Michigan Senator‑elect Abdul El‑Sayed says he’s open to working with Trump on healthcare
content: Newly elected Democratic Michigan senator Abdul El-Sayed stated on Sunday that he is open to collaborating with President Trump on affordable healthcare. This willingness to work together comes despite the two figures exchanging verbal jabs during El-Sayed’s campaign. El-Sayed noted that he has never met the president, emphasizing Trump’s role as the sitting head of state and his own status as the U.S. Senator-elect.
summary: Abdul El‑Sayed, the newly elected Democratic Michigan senator, said on Sunday he is open to working with President Trump on affordable healthcare. He noted the two have traded jabs while he was on the campaign trail.
author: The Hill

title: Katie Miller pauses podcast after Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff
content: Katie Miller, a conservative influencer, stated she is pausing her podcast following the selection of her husband, Stephen Miller, as White House chief of staff. In a Sunday statement, Miller explained that her decision was based on what is best for her children and family as Stephen Miller takes on his new role for President Trump.
summary: Katie Miller paused her podcast after her husband Stephen Miller was selected as White House chief of staff. She said she is stepping back from the show on Sunday to focus on her children and family.
author: The Hill

title: Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda calls Democratic majority an opportunity for Trump
content: Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda (D-N. C.) stated on Sunday that the Democrats’ upcoming congressional majority offers President Trump an opportunity to collaborate on legislation aimed at improving Americans’ lives. Ojeda warned that failing to push for bills that elevate people’s lives in Washington, D.C., would result in a loss.
summary: Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda calls Democratic majority an opportunity for Trump.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says his immigration crackdown may have been too tough after midterm losses
content: President Trump said on Sunday that his deportation policies might have been too tough and may have contributed to the GOP’s historic losses in this year’s elections. CBS News’s Ross Douthat asked him on “60 Minutes” whether his immigration policy cost the party the midterms, to which Trump replied that the policy both helped and hurt.
summary: Trump says his immigration crackdown may have been too tough after midterm losses.
author: The Hill

title: Western Canadian Farmers Must Manage Soil Acidity Across Entire Rotations
content: Long-term research from the University of Alberta indicates that Western Canadian farmers should manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation, rather than on a crop-by-crop basis, to protect future harvests.
summary: Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation to protect future harvests. This recommendation comes from long‑term research conducted by the University of Alberta.
author: Phys.org

title: Ottawa study finds 26.7‑billion‑year‑old universe model passes cosmology tests
content: A new University of Ottawa study reports that an alternative cosmological model, which posits a 26.7-billion-year-old universe without dark matter or dark energy, has passed several major cosmology tests. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," has been published in the journal Universe.
summary: A University of Ottawa study reports that a 26.7‑billion‑year‑old universe model without dark matter or dark energy passes several major cosmology tests. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," appears in the journal Universe.
author: Phys.org

title: Medieval Public Health System in Trondheim Exposes Population to Roundworm
content: A medieval public health system introduced in Trondheim unintentionally exposed residents to roundworm. While the program involved deliberate sanitation interventions, it had the opposite effect, increasing disease spread in the city.
summary: Medieval health and sanitation efforts in Trondheim involved deliberate interventions. Some of these measures increased the spread of disease, exposing the population to roundworm.
author: Phys.org

title: Heavy rain can more than double glacier speeds in Alaska
content: Glaciers, typically viewed as slow-moving ice masses that carve landscapes via gravity, can occasionally experience rapid surges increasing their speed by orders of magnitude. This phenomenon, where unyielding blocks of ice transition from a slow crawl to a fast surge, highlights the variable nature of glacial movement.
summary: Glaciers normally move slowly downhill by gravity, carving the landscape. Occasionally, they surge, moving orders of magnitude faster than their usual speed.
author: Phys.org

title: New tiny jellyfish species Copula lucentia discovered off Alicante, Spain
content:
Scientists have identified a new jellyfish species, Copula lucentia, in the Mediterranean Sea. The tiny medusa, measuring only a few millimeters, was found off the coast of El Campello in Alicante.

The species was formally described in 2024 by a research team from the University of Alicante’s Marine Laboratory in Dénia. The laboratory is part of the university’s Ramón Margalef Multidisciplinary Institute for Environmental Research.
summary: Copula lucentia is a tiny jellyfish measuring just a few millimeters, discovered off El Campello in Alicante, Spain. It was formally described in 2024 by a research team at the University of Alicante Marine Laboratory in Dénia, part of the university's Ramón Margalef Multidisciplinary Institute for Environmental Research.
author: Phys.org

title: Kyushu University researchers find H3mm15 histone variant essential for mouse sperm development
content:
Kyushu University researchers discovered H3mm15, a histone H3.3 subvariant, is essential for normal sperm development in mice by regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis.  

The study shows H3mm15 cannot replace conventional H3.3; despite only three amino acid differences, the two proteins behave differently within chromatin, the DNA‑protein structure that packages genetic material.
summary: Kyushu University researchers find H3mm15 histone variant essential for mouse sperm development.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Tokyo researchers find hidden earthquake traces in Kumano Sea sediment
content:
Researchers at the University of Tokyo have applied a new type of radiocarbon analysis to a sediment core taken from the Kumano Sea off Japan’s coast. The study, published in the journal Radiocarbon, uncovered multiple “hidden” traces of previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough.

The findings add detail to the seismic history of the region, where a future megaquake is anticipated. By reconstructing a more accurate picture of past seismic activity, the research aims to improve predictions of future geophysical events and aid in disaster preparedness.
summary: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have used a new type of radiocarbon analysis to study a sediment core taken from the Kumano Sea off the coast of Japan. This has revealed multiple "hidden" traces of previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough, where the country's next megaquake is expected to occur.
author: Phys.org

title: New simulation model enhances nursing staff empowerment and autonomy
content: A new clinical simulation model has been introduced to strengthen the empowerment and autonomy of nursing staff. Unlike traditional methods that mainly assess technical skills and compliance with medical standards from a generic, interprofessional view, this model emphasizes nursing‑specific aspects such as care ethics, relational presence with patients, and emotional management among nurses.
summary: A new clinical simulation model strengthens the empowerment and autonomy of nursing staff. Previous simulation methods mainly assessed technical skills and compliance, overlooking care ethics, relational presence, and emotional management.
author: Phys.org

title: Dead star's double ring of planetary wreckage offers preview of Sun's future
content:
Astronomers have discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, offering a possible preview of what might happen to our Solar System in the distant future.

The two rings are separated by a mysterious gap that researchers believe is maintained by surviving planetary bodies, including one potentially as large as Pluto or the Moon.

Their different chemical compositions suggest they may contain the remains of separate destroyed planets.
summary: Astronomers discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star. The rings are separated by a gap maintained by surviving bodies, possibly as large as Pluto or the Moon, and their different chemical compositions suggest they contain remains of destroyed planets.
author: Science Daily

title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
content:
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way from preliminary observations that cover only 7 % of the night sky.  

The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy located 355,000 light‑years away and a star cluster concealed behind cosmic dust.  

Scientists believe that hundreds of additional satellite galaxies may still be hidden, and the Observatory’s powerful telescope could eventually reveal them.
summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky.
author: Science Daily

title: UC San Francisco scientists develop brain‑specific therapy that eliminates tumors in mice
content: UC San Francisco scientists developed a new cancer therapy that stays inactive until it reaches the brain, where it activates to attack tumors. The therapy uses engineered immune cells called B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells. In two mouse models, the B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma (DMG), an aggressive childhood brain cancer that is almost always fatal within a year.
summary: UC San Francisco scientists created B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells that activate only in the brain to target tumors. In two mouse models, the therapy completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma, a fatal childhood brain cancer.
author: Science Daily

title: Einstein's Equations Reveal Gravitational Reconnection That Releases Energy
content:
Scientists have identified a new phenomenon hidden in Einstein’s equations. Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez describe a theoretical process called gravitational reconnection.

In this process, structures within gravitational fields can break apart and then reconnect, transferring energy into matter. The discovery suggests gravity can release energy through such reconnections, a behavior not previously highlighted in Einstein’s framework.
summary: Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez identified a theoretical process called gravitational reconnection, in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter. The process transfers energy into matter.
author: Science Daily

title: New Amazon fish species Laimosemion laranja discovered, already endangered
content:
Researchers discovered a new species of tiny orange‑patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon. The killifish, named Laimosemion laranja, measures less than three centimeters and was found in only three small forest pools.  

Its limited habitat faces threats from mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.
summary: Researchers discovered a tiny orange-patterned fish, Laimosemion laranja, in the Brazilian Amazon. The species, less than three centimeters long and found only in three small forest pools, faces habitat threats from mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.
author: Science Daily

title: Sticky marine snow can move over six times more carbon to the deep ocean
content: Scientists have found that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” significantly affects how much carbon sinks to the deep ocean. Because gooier particles are less readily broken down by bacteria, they can carry more than six times the carbon to depth, highlighting an unexpected link between ocean slime and the planet’s climate.
summary: Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” plays an important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean. Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected link between ocean slime and Earth's climate.
author: Science Daily

title: Colombian fossil discovery reveals "Biotic Inflection" in ancient ocean
content: A remarkable fossil discovery in Colombia is challenging how scientists understand major evolutionary changes in Earth's history. Researchers uncovered an incredibly diverse ancient marine ecosystem where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged. They call this previously unrecognized pattern a "Biotic Inflection," suggesting that major transformations in life can occur without mass extinctions.
summary: Scientists discovered a diverse ancient marine ecosystem in Colombia where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged. They named this previously unrecognized pattern the "Biotic Inflection," indicating that major evolutionary transformations can occur without mass extinctions.
author: Science Daily

title: Protein Miro1 buildup linked to insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
content: Scientists have identified a protein called Miro1 as a potential driver of insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes. Preclinical experiments demonstrated that removing this protein restores muscle response to insulin. Additionally, research found that exercise lowers Miro1 levels in people with diabetes, suggesting a new pathway for treating the disease.
summary: Scientists found that a buildup of the protein Miro1 may drive insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes, with preclinical experiments showing that removing it restores muscle response to insulin. Exercise was also found to lower Miro1 levels in people with diabetes, revealing a potential new treatment pathway.
author: Science Daily

title: Jensen Huang Sends Memo to Nvidia Employees Acknowledging Affair
content:
Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., appeared at a media briefing in Tokyo on Thursday, July 16 2026, following the company’s “Japan AI Ecosystem” reception. The event highlighted Nvidia’s ongoing engagement with Japan’s technology community.

Japan announced plans to purchase 27,500 next‑generation Rubin chips from Nvidia to support the development of a domestic foundational AI model for robots. The purchase is part of Japan’s broader strategy to build homegrown AI capabilities.

On Sunday, Nvidia disclosed that it had begun an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, an AI executive and agent of the Chinese government. The Board of Directors announced the investigation, and Huang sent a memo to Nvidia employees acknowledging the affair. The memo began: “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent a memo to employees apologizing for being unfaithful to his wife. The company announced it is investigating his relationship with Alice Huang, an AI executive and Chinese government agent.
author: The Verge

title: US offers $20 million reward and possible relocation for info on Iran’s nuclear program
content: The U.S. State Department announced a $20 million reward and potential relocation assistance for information regarding Iran’s nuclear program. The announcement cited the regime’s failure to comply with IAEA safeguards obligations, which the department stated resulted in the agency losing "continuity of knowledge."
summary: The State Department announced a $20 million reward and possible relocation for information on Iran’s nuclear program. It also said the regime’s lack of compliance with IAEA safeguards has caused the agency to lose continuity of knowledge.
author: Euronews

title: US launches new targeted strikes on Iran as Trump claims progress in talks with Tehran
content: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems, sending ripples across the Gulf, but Trump insists they are “minor strikes” while intense diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all-out war.
summary: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems. Trump insists the strikes are minor while diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all‑out war.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV Welcomed by 40,000 in Paysandú, Uruguay
content: The Pontiff was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. Leo's sixth apostolic journey comes less than a month after lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
summary: Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. The visit is his sixth apostolic journey and occurs less than a month after his lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
author: Euronews

title: Video shows people fleeing during gunman shooting in Kraków, Poland
content: Video footage captured on user‑generated content shows people running for cover amid a deadly shooting in Kraków, Poland. According to police, the incident has resulted in at least six fatalities and around a dozen injuries.
summary: UGC footage shows people running for cover during a deadly shooting in Kraków, Poland. Police say at least six people were killed and around a dozen were wounded.
author: Euronews

title: Russian strikes damage Kyiv region infrastructure, ruin kindergarten in capital
content: Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.
summary: Russian strikes damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.
author: Euronews

title: Footage shows gunman shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square, six dead
content: Footage captured a shooting at Krakow’s Main Market Square, showing a gunman opening fire. People were seen taking cover and fleeing while cars sped away. The attack left six people dead and about 15 injured.
summary: Footage shows people fleeing and cars speeding away during a shooting at Krakow's Main Market Square. The incident left six people dead and about 15 injured.
author: Euronews

title: Trump offers UFC head Dana White White House press secretary role
content: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.
summary: President Trump reportedly offered Dana White, head of the UFC, the role of White House press secretary. Media reports say White has already turned down the offer.
author: France 24

title: Israeli President Herzog Tasks Gadi Eisenkot to Form Government
content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after neither Eisenkot’s bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a clear majority in the October 27 elections.  

Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to assemble a coalition government.  Follow our liveblog to see how the day’s events unfold.
summary: On Sunday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government. Eisenkot has up to six weeks to build a coalition after neither his bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a clear majority in the October 27 elections.
author: France 24

title: Paraguay Senate Impeaches President Santiago Peña After He Offered Resignation
content:
Paraguay’s Senate impeached ousted President Santiago Peña instead of accepting his offer to resign. Peña was charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank, an online bank where regulators seized control after nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts. While repayments are currently underway, protests persist as customers continue to demand access to their funds.

Peña, who denies any wrongdoing, was initially placed under house arrest before being transferred to a military facility for his own safety.
summary: Paraguay's Senate impeached ousted president Santiago Peña after he offered to resign, and he has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. He was moved from house arrest to a military facility for safety while nearly three million customers remain locked out of their accounts, with repayments beginning amid protests; Peña denies any wrongdoing.
author: France 24

title: Diwali celebrations see over one billion participants worldwide
content: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. According to the headline, over one billion people are observing the festival as a victory of light over darkness. In Ayodhya, the site traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Lord Rama, festivities featured performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, along with laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
summary: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday as people across India and the global diaspora gathered for the Hindu festival. In Ayodhya, believed to be Lord Rama's birthplace, events featured Ramayana performances, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
author: France 24

title: Senegal Wins Two Beach Wrestling Golds at 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games
content: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.
summary: Senegal secured two gold medals in beach wrestling at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won the -55 kg gold, the host country’s first Youth Olympic gold, and Maguette Diop won gold in the -80 kg category.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina, criticises Milei's three-year austerity
content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his tour began, becoming the first pontiff to visit the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades. He faced calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei, publicly criticizing that policy and stating that economic growth must benefit all.
summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday, after beginning his tour in Uruguay. The first papal visit to the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades, he criticised President Javier Milei’s three‑year austerity programme and said economic growth must benefit all.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia board to investigate reports Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
content: Nvidia’s board announced on Sunday it will investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive that U.S. intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
summary: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing, and he will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
author: France 24

title: Trump vows political comeback after GOP loses Congress, Democrats pledge accountability
content: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he intends to make a political comeback after Republicans lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Incoming Democratic leaders said they will hold his administration to account, while the attorney general pledged to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.
summary: President Donald Trump said on Sunday he will seek a political comeback after Republicans lost control of Congress in the recent midterm elections. Incoming Democratic leaders said they will hold his administration to account, and the attorney general promised to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.
author: France 24

title: Gaza siblings born without legs receive first personal chair
content:
In Gaza, 10‑year‑old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand. They struggle to move around and to perform daily tasks such as eating and writing independently.

For the first time, one of the siblings has their own chair, a development that brings a new sense of freedom to the family.
summary: In Gaza, 10‑year‑old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand. The children struggle to move around and perform daily activities such as eating and writing independently.
author: UN News

title: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom
content: On his way to school in Vienna on the morning of 10 November 1938, eight-year-old Arthur Schneier watched his synagogue burn while firefighters and police officers stood by “rejoicing”.
summary: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom.
author: UN News

title: GPs to provide extra support to 300,000 vulnerable patients in £40m NHS winter scheme
content:
A £40 million scheme in England will provide extra support to vulnerable patients in an effort to ease winter pressure on the NHS. Family doctors will extend services to 300,000 people with frailty and long‑term conditions, offering health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests aimed at preventing avoidable hospital admissions.

The programme is intended to keep most vulnerable individuals well at home and reduce unnecessary stays in hospital as the NHS prepares for the coming months’ demands.
summary: A £40 million scheme in England will have family doctors offer extra support to 300,000 vulnerable patients this winter. The support includes health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests aimed at preventing avoidable hospital admissions.
author: Guardian World

title: Education Secretary Lucy Powell warns early GCSE teaching may turn schools into exam factories
content: Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education. Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.
summary: Education Secretary Lucy Powell warns early GCSE teaching may turn schools into exam factories.
author: Guardian World

title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons
content: ‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years. The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.
summary: Maya Jama, a 32‑year‑old presenter, announced on Instagram that she is leaving her role as host of Love Island. She said it is time to throw herself into something new after three years on the show.
author: Guardian World

title: Earthshot prize ceremony set for Reliance-owned Jio World Centre in Mumbai, draws criticism
content:
Conservation groups have voiced criticism of the venue chosen for the Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize awards. The ceremony will be held on 17 November at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai, a facility owned by Reliance Industries, the conglomerate of the Ambani family that operates the world’s largest oil refinery and funds a controversial mega‑zoo.  

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which grants £1 million each year to five winners for conservation projects, confirmed the location to the Guardian and Mongabay. The criticism centres on Reliance’s fossil‑fuel interests and the zoo project linked to its foundation.
summary: The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will hold its annual awards ceremony on 17 November at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. Conservationists have criticised the venue because it is owned by Reliance Industries, which runs the world’s biggest oil refinery and funds a controversial mega‑zoo.
author: Guardian World

title: Court rejects Home Office claim asylum seeker ransom kidnapping not trafficking
content:
The Court of Appeal rejected the Home Office’s claim that kidnapping for ransom does not constitute exploitation of trafficking victims. The decision was reached in a case involving a Syrian man who was abducted in Libya.

With the ruling, people who have been kidnapped for ransom—previously excluded from the definition of trafficking victims—will now have their claims considered. Those individuals may become eligible for the support and recovery package that is available to recognized trafficking victims.
summary: Court rejects Home Office claim asylum seeker ransom kidnapping not trafficking.
author: Guardian World

title: President Isaac Herzog tasks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israeli government
content: Israel’s president has tasked Yashar party leader Gadi Eiskont with attempting to form a new government after the Knesset remained deadlocked following last month’s election, which saw Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lose its majority.
